scope: Domain B (patents, 7 sources) + Domain E (customs/trade, 10 sources)
headline: Trade: three open sources verified (UN Comtrade preview, Eurostat Comext, HMRC UK Trade Info) and one of them is company-level. Patents: ZERO records obtainable without registration or payment - the patent component of this round is a scoping result, not a data result.

detail: Not a single patent record was obtained in this round. Every patent path reachable from this host was credential-gated, paid, or dead, and each was probed live rather than assumed.

EPO OPS: both /published-data/search and /family/... returned HTTP 403 with '403This request has been rejected due to the violation of Fair Use policy'; the OAuth2 token endpoint also refused (401). Nothing readable without a registered app.
USPTO Open Data Portal: /api/v1/patent/applications/search and /api/v1/datasets/products/... both returned HTTP 401 {"message":"Unauthorized"}. A free X-API-KEY is required.

PatentsView: the documented host search.patentsview.org does not resolve (NXDOMAIN from the system resolver and from 8.8.8.8); the legacy host api.patentsview.org returns HTTP 200 but an HTML single-page-app shell, not JSON. The service is retired and its surface now serves the USPTO ODP app. There is nothing to fetch and nothing to register for.

USPTO bulk: bulkdata.uspto.gov no longer resolves (DNS returns only an SOA record); data.uspto.gov/bulkdata is the ODP shell and the surviving dataset-product API is key-gated (401/403). Zero bytes of bulk data were downloaded.
WIPO PATENTSCOPE: no open interface. The search UI is a JSF web app; an undocumented /search/api/ path is 404; PCT data products are routed to a subscription page.
Google Patents on BigQuery: bigquery.googleapis.com returns 401 anonymously. Public data can be queried within a free 1 TB/month allowance, but that still needs a GCP project and OAuth credentials.
Lens.org: the API is institutional-subscription only ('Lens API service is only available through an institutional subscription', from its own terms page) and returns 401 without a token.
Consequence for MedRadar: there is currently no patent data, so no patent-derived lead-time, technology-trend or citation analysis can be computed. Do not let any report imply otherwise.

Cheapest route out (not taken here because it needs an account, which the protocol forbids): a free USPTO ODP API key, and/or a free EPO OPS registration. Both are documentable in a few hours once someone may create the accounts.

2_five_firm_patent_and_trade_linkage.patents: IDENTICAL FOR ALL FIVE AND CURRENTLY NIL. With no patent data, no firm has a patent link. When a key arrives: patent applicants are legal strings, so parent names ('MEDTRONIC', 'KONINKLIJKE PHILIPS N.V.') resolve as exact_alias through identity.CompanyIndex, while subsidiaries ('MEDTRONIC VASCULAR INC', 'GE HEALTHCARE FINNAMORE LIMITED') need manual alias additions or stay candidate. Neither EPO OPS nor USPTO ODP provides a disambiguated assignee id, so expect a large candidate tier. PatentsView's assignee_id - the one feature that solved this - is gone with the service.

trade.general: Only UK HMRC offers an open company-level channel, and it is presence-only (no values, no quantities, no partners). No other open source names a company at all. Bill-of-lading vendors (ImportGenius, Panjiva, Datamyne) would provide the real firm-level shipment evidence but are all paid.

notable_findings: PATENTS ARE UNOBTAINABLE WITHOUT AN ACCOUNT: 0 patent records from 7 patent sources. Everything is credential-gated, paid or dead. This is the single most important negative result of my scope.

PatentsView IS GONE, not merely key-gated: search.patentsview.org is NXDOMAIN (two resolvers), api.patentsview.org/patents/query returns HTTP 200 but an HTML SPA shell, and patentsview.org's own meta description says 'The Open Data Portal (ODP) is USPTO's data platform'. Counting patentsview and uspto_open_data_portal as two independent sources would double-count one authority - and SOURCE_ID_INDEX still lists PatentsView as a separate P0 with a dead URL.

bulkdata.uspto.gov NO LONGER RESOLVES, so the classic free multi-TB patent bulk channel does not exist here; the only surviving bulk path is the keyed ODP dataset API. I downloaded 0 bytes of bulk data.

US CENSUS RETURNS HTTP 200 ON FAILURE: keyless calls yield a 200 text/html page titled 'Missing Key'. Any client that trusts status codes will silently parse an error page as data. This is the most dangerous trap found.

UN COMTRADE HAS TWO DISTINCT CAPABILITIES that must be reported separately: the anonymous /public/v1/preview endpoint works (278 real partner rows for HS 9018/9022/9402 in the saved samples) while the full /data/v1 endpoint is 401 without a subscription key.

HMRC UK TRADE INFO IS THE ONLY OPEN COMPANY-LEVEL TRADE CHANNEL FOUND: api.uktradeinfo.com is open OData with no key, and its Trader entity exposes CompanyName + PostCode joined to CN8 commodity and month. It is PRESENCE ONLY - no values, no quantities, no partners, no consignments. It is not a bill of lading and must never be reported as one.

ALL FIVE TARGET FIRMS HAVE UK TRADER ENTITIES in HMRC data (Medtronic 4, Philips 3, Draeger 3, GE HealthCare 2, Mindray 1), so a company-level UK clock is genuinely possible - but names are raw declarant strings with typos ('PHILIPS PHILIPHS'), and several non-UK traders share HMRC's own address/postcode AB10 1ZP, so address cannot disambiguate.

THE SHARED ALIAS TABLE OVER-MATCHES FOR TRADE: 'PHILIPS IN LIGHTING LTD' and 'PHILIPS CONSUMER LIFESTYLE BV' resolve as exact_alias to Philips because the negative guards only cover 'PHILIPS LIGHTING' as consecutive tokens. My connector adds an explicit trade demotion guard (LIGHTING / CONSUMER LIFESTYLE / LUMILEDS / SIGNIFY / SAFETY) so these become candidates, never confirmed links.

EUROSTAT COMEXT NEEDS THE RIGHT PATH AND DIMENSIONS: the dataset lives under /api/comext/dissemination/... (the mainstream /api/dissemination/ path returns 404 for DS-045409) and its dimensions are freq/reporter/partner/product/flow/indicators/time - using geo= returns 400.

BIGQUERY IS NOT 'PAID_ONLY': the public-data page states the first 1 TB per month is free and billing is only required beyond the free tier. It is still REQUIRES_REGISTRATION because a GCP project and OAuth credentials are mandatory. (I corrected this after re-reading the saved page.)

EPO OPS QUOTA IS UNVERIFIED: the docs page we could fetch does not state a volume, and developers.epo.org answered 403 to our client, so I removed the '4 GB/month' figure rather than repeat an unverified number.

IMPORTYETI IS A POLICY BLOCK, NOT A TECHNICAL ONE: robots.txt disallows exactly the path that answers the question (/search?q) plus the JSON API paths. Zero data requests were made; do not build a scraper for it.

AGGREGATE vs SHIPMENT IS ENFORCED IN CODE: all aggregate connectors emit an empty entity_refs list and a null canonical_key, so an HS-code statistic cannot accidentally acquire a company link downstream.
time_semantics_rules_for_reviewers: PATENTS: source_public_at = publication date (the 18-month public disclosure), never filing or priority. Filing/priority is event_at only. A not-yet-published application is not public and must never be treated as an early signal. OPS exposes date-publ/date-filing/priority separately; ODP exposes publicationDate/filingDate/grantDate separately.
PATENTSVIEW would have been a GRANT-date clock only (no pre-grant publication field), so it could not have served as a public-visibility clock even before retirement.

TRADE AGGREGATES (Comtrade/Census/Eurostat/HMRC-OTS): no source exposes a per-record publication timestamp. Every record is therefore written with source_public_at = '' and quality 'unknown', and event_at is a derived period anchor. These records must be excluded from any lead-time computation.
HMRC TRADER PRESENCE: month/year precision only, published in arrears by HMRC, with no publication date in the API. Same rule: source_public_at unknown, not lead-time eligible.
No record anywhere in my scope was given a fabricated publication clock. If a downstream report needs a knowledge clock for trade, that clock does not exist in the data and must be stated as missing.
warnings_for_lead: Do not report '17 trade/patent sources, 3 verified' as if patents had a foothold: the 3 verified sources are ALL trade. Patents: 0 verified, 0 records.
Do not merge patentsview with uspto_open_data_portal in any coverage count; they are one retired authority and one live one.
Do not describe HMRC trader data as shipment data; it is company-level presence with no values.
Do not compare aggregate HS statistics with bill-of-lading totals; different coverage, thresholds, valuation and confidentiality rules make them non-comparable.

SOURCE_ID_INDEX has two dead official_url values in my scope: patentsview (search.patentsview.org) and descartes_datamyne (descartes.com/solutions/global-trade-data). Both are documented in the register records; the index itself was not modified (out of my write scope).

If the Lead authorises account creation, the two highest-value registrations are a free USPTO ODP key (unlocks US application/publication search) and a free EPO OPS app (unlocks publication date + family + citations). Both are free; neither is a purchase.

open_questions: Does anything in the repo already assume patent data exists (e.g. a template that joins patents to devices)? If so it must be guarded, because there is no patent data.
Should SOURCE_ID_INDEX be corrected for the two dead URLs (patentsview, descartes_datamyne) and for the PatentsView/ODP duplication? That is outside my write scope; the Lead owns the index.

If accounts become permissible next round, which is worth more: US pre-grant publications (ODP, free key, US-centric) or EP/PCT publication + family + citations (EPO OPS, free app, global)? They answer different questions and neither is a substitute for the other.

For firm-level trade evidence beyond the UK, the only route is a paid BoL vendor. Is the research question strong enough to justify a quote from S&P or ImportGenius, given that the licence will forbid redistributing records?

HMRC presence could be extended to more CN8 codes and all five firms' UK entities cheaply (free). Worth doing only if a firm-level UK clock is actually used in an experiment - otherwise it is data with no consumer.
